topic: Prompt of the week: the "is this message legit?" red-flag checker (after a $129M AI impersonation case)
post:
Got an urgent message from your "boss" asking for money or passwords? 🚩
This prompt helps you spot the red flags before you act.

Why this week:
Federal prosecutors charged three men in an alleged $129 million scheme that used AI to impersonate CEOs and lawyers, per AP and ITPro. Fake voices and faces are getting convincing.

Prompt of the week 👇
Remove names, account numbers and personal details first, then paste:

"Here is a message I received: [paste it]. List every red flag you see, like urgency, secrecy, unusual payment requests, or changes to bank details. Then tell me exactly how to verify it through a separate channel I already trust. Don't tell me it's safe. Tell me what to check."

What you get:
✅ A list of warning signs
✅ A verification plan
✅ A moment to pause before you act

The key line: "Don't tell me it's safe." AI can't confirm who really sent a message. Only a call-back to a number you already know can. ☎️

Why it matters:
Scams work by rushing you. This prompt buys you 30 seconds of clear thinking. 💡

Practical takeaway:
Never approve a payment from a call, email or video alone. Always confirm through a second channel.
